question: Can the published PGCN TEV design validation provide a frozen prospective intended-bond benchmark and a fair released comparison with a sequence-only baseline?

decision_changing_outcomes.continue: Exact released training/design/test membership, pre-outcome selection of the paired validation cases, intended-bond-resolved outcomes, and predictions from PGCN plus a competent sequence baseline on the same cases would support a method comparison.
decision_changing_outcomes.stop: Missing exact membership, outcome-conditioned case selection, a cleavage-only reporter, or no aligned released baseline closes this route without model execution.

paper.citation: Lu et al., Prediction and design of protease enzyme specificity using a structure-aware graph convolutional network, PNAS 120 e2303590120 (2023)
relevant_sections: Results: Experimental Evaluation of PGCN Generalizability Using Protease Design
Materials and Methods: Combinatorial Library Preparation and Yeast-Surface Display
Materials and Methods: Library FACS and cytometric analysis of individual designs

release.relationship_to_paper: The audited commit postdates the paper's 2023-09-20 online publication and cannot by itself establish a pre-assay freeze.

released_split_audit.paper_report: The source cleavage data were randomly split 80/10/10; reported TEV totals are 4340 training, 542 validation and 543 test examples.
released_split_audit.release_expectation: README.md names ind.<dataset>.trisplit.test.index and ind.<dataset>.trisplit.val.index as the files carrying exact membership.
released_split_audit.github_observation: The GitHub tree does not contain the TEV graph tensors, sequence-order arrays, or the named split-index files. TestIndexSelection.ipynb regenerates membership with np.random.shuffle but records aggregate counts rather than the membership arrays.
released_split_audit.zenodo_recovery: The paper-linked Zenodo record 7653923 contains train_val_test_graph_datasets.zip. Six bounded HTTP range responses totaling 106602 bytes recovered the archived TEV test and validation indices plus labels and sequence identities without downloading the 897469246-byte archive.
released_split_audit.conclusion: Exact membership is recoverable from the paper-linked archive and matches the published aggregate counts. The random split is pair-disjoint but permits substrate identity to cross protease variants; it is historical specificity evidence, not the final design-panel comparator.

design_chronology.prospective_component: A pretrained PGCN scored 280 P2-targeted and 4320 P6-targeted Rosetta designs before the YESS experiment. The paper reports selecting 200 and 126 by predicted cleavage probability, then 18 and 96 energetically favorable designs for combinatorial-library construction.
design_chronology.outcome_conditioning: The exact 19 reported clonal cases were selected after FACS outcomes: nine from the cleaved pool and ten from the uncleaved pool.
design_chronology.cohort_scope_conflict: The paper describes the 19 clones as selected from P6- and P2-targeted pools, but released Table S8 contains three P3-targeted negative controls. The stated P6/P2 campaign subset is therefore 16 cases, not all 19.

listed_source_externality.boundary: This establishes exact-identity externality from the listed source table, not an exact checkpoint split or a pre-outcome frozen pair-level test. KNLYFQ and ENLYYQ motifs do occur with other P1-prime residues and protease backgrounds, so exact-target absence is not motif-level novelty.

design_chronology.conclusion: The work is a prospectively model-guided library-enrichment experiment, but the displayed 19-pair evaluation is outcome-conditioned rather than a frozen prospective pair-level benchmark.

assay_endpoint.method: YESS tag-loss reporter with anti-HA and anti-FLAG fluorescence, FACS isolation of cleaved and uncleaved pools, and flow-cytometry clonal validation.
assay_endpoint.supported: Binary reporter cleavage classification under the assay conditions.
not_supported: Direct product mapping to the intended Q/A bond by mass spectrometry or N-terminomics
A calibrated rate, catalytic efficiency, product distribution, or off-target specificity measurement
assay_endpoint.conclusion: The endpoint is useful broad cleavage evidence but does not meet the intended-bond requirement for this Problem 8 benchmark.

baseline_audit.released_alignment: Table S8 contains mutation, target position, YESS class, PGCN class and PGCN confidence for the 19 clones; it has no sequence-baseline prediction column.
baseline_audit.notebook_observation: BenchmarkMLTrainigAfterPGCN.ipynb contains post-hoc design-set ML comparison attempts, but referenced logits and generated reports point to unreleased scratch paths and do not provide an exact aligned 19-clone sequence-baseline result.
baseline_audit.design_stage_confound: PGCN probability, Rosetta energetic favorability, visual inspection and mutation enrichment all contribute to the tested combinatorial libraries. With no matched sequence-only, Rosetta-only or random/frequency-matched design arm, assay outcomes cannot isolate the PGCN contribution.
baseline_audit.confidence_discrepancy: Released Table S8 contains two measured-positive rows with PGCN confidence 0.6054516435 and 0.6923581958, whereas the paper text states that all nine cleaved designs were predicted with probability greater than 0.75.
baseline_audit.conclusion: A fair released PGCN-versus-sequence-baseline comparison on the exact clonal cases is not executable.

decision.conclusion: The published validation supports prospective PGCN-guided library enrichment and broad binary reporter cleavage on new exact protease identities. It does not supply a frozen exact-pair prospective benchmark, intended-bond-resolved outcomes, or an aligned released sequence baseline.
decision.stopping_rule: Met. Do not run or retrain PGCN for a clean method-selection claim from these 19 clones, do not treat outcome-selected clones as a prospective test set, and do not relabel tag loss as intended-bond validation.
decision.strongest_feasible_alternative: Retain this study as source-supported qualitative library-enrichment evidence. For method selection, require a different public panel whose cases were fixed before outcomes, whose products identify the intended cleavage bond, and whose exact inputs support both a structure-aware method and a competent sequence baseline.
decision.next_question: Does a public cleavage-site-resolved protease design study release a pre-outcome candidate list with exact sequences, paired positive and negative outcomes, and enough inputs to score the same cases with both structure-aware and sequence baselines?
decision.next_stop: Stop source acquisition after one bounded survey if no study exposes all four elements; convert the missing bond-resolved prospective panel into an explicit external assay/data dependency rather than weakening the endpoint.

source_acquisition.operation: Three public Git clone/fetch sequences across scheduled runs, each resolving the same release commit, plus bounded paper/Zenodo metadata and ZIP-member range reads. The 897469246-byte archive was not downloaded in full.
source_acquisition.accounting_boundary: The known shell-transfer lower bound is below the 31457280-byte batch cap. Exact Git smart-HTTP framing, one unsaved Zenodo metadata response, preliminary probes, and connector/web transport bytes are not exposed, so this is not certified exact wire-byte accounting.
source_acquisition.relationship_to_other_batches: Distinct method-reproducibility question; it does not reset or consume the retained Chen-v3 or TEV L2F source batches.
